leads.raw_title: Fitbit founders launch Luffu Link, an LTE health and safety band
leads.raw_description: Luffu, founded by Fitbit co-founders James Park and Eric Friedman, launched preorder availability for Luffu Link, a screenless LTE-enabled band combining all-day health sensing, voice logging, GPS/location awareness, family check-ins and help requests without a nearby phone. leads.raw_title: Fashion startup Atorie raises $9.5M to bring consumers luxury goods without the markup
leads.raw_description: Atorie is an AI-powered fashion marketplace connecting factory-owned brands and luxury manufacturers directly with consumers. TechCrunch reported a $9.5 million seed round, around $5 million in sales in the prior year, a company expectation of an annualized run rate above $55 million in 2026, and work with more than 40 factories. The platform uses AI for trend analysis, demand and material-shortage estimates, color testing, outfit building and personalized suggestions; it also plans an in-house line and creator or influencer clothing lines.

leads.raw_title: Hoomanely's building a smart feeding bowl and an AI platform to help owners spot when their pup is sick
leads.raw_description: Palo Alto startup Hoomanely offers EverBowl, a sensor-equipped dog feeding station and app subscription that measure food and water intake, eating speed, chewing and swallowing sounds, facial thermal readings and oral motion. Its AI establishes an individual baseline and surfaces prolonged deviations. TechCrunch reported an 18-month beta covering more than 80 dogs and about 5 million data points, roughly 50 devices shipped, a $29-per-month service, and $1.8 million in pre-seed funding. Hoomanely describes a longer-term animal-health data model serving research, nutrition and insurance companies.

leads.raw_title: Two years after launch, Walmart's Flipkart is closing in on India's quick-commerce leaders
leads.raw_description: Flipkart Minutes, launched in August 2024, was reported to be delivering 1.1 million to 1.2 million orders per day, up from about 390,000 to 400,000 in November. TechCrunch reported roughly 1,020 to 1,050 micro-fulfillment centers, up from 600 in January and about 340 a year earlier, with around 100 facilities being added monthly and a 1,500-center target by end-2026. Reported repeat-buyer share was 65% to 70%, transactions per customer were up 50% to 60% year over year, average delivery time fell to about 11 minutes from 13, and average order value was about ₹400 to ₹500.

leads.raw_description: easyGroup and UK marketplace technology company OnBuy announced easyShop.com, a planned value-led, pure online marketplace for millions of products including clothing, accessories, footwear and beauty.
